1	"""Write-ahead log key value store.
2	
3	Every mutation is first appended to a framed log. A commit marker is the
4	only thing that advances the durable sequence number. When a store is opened,
5	any tail that was never committed (including a record torn by a hard kill) is
6	discarded, so recovery always yields exactly the committed state.
7	
8	Only the very last log record may be incomplete: a process killed while
9	appending leaves at most one torn record, which is dropped without being
10	applied. Any other framing failure -- a truncated record in the middle, a
11	length field out of bounds, unparseable content, or a duplicate/regressing
12	commit sequence -- is corruption, and recovery raises ``CorruptLogError``
13	without touching the store.
14	
15	Recovery itself may be killed at any point, any number of times. Two small
16	sidecar files in the store directory, both maintained below the write path,
17	make the convergence protocol kill-safe and its report stable:
18	
19	``wal.ckp``
20	    A byte-for-byte copy of the log prefix ending at the most recent commit
21	    marker, replaced atomically (temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync)
22	    only after that commit frame is durable. A log torn at *any* offset --
23	    even offset 0, or inside the committed prefix -- is rebuilt from it, so
24	    the durable sequence number never regresses. It is also the published
25	    snapshot read-only processes pin (see below).
26	
27	``wal.rec``
28	    A recovery marker written only after a log needing repair has passed
29	    full validation and only *before* the atomic rebuild starts. It records
30	    the clean prefix length and whether a torn record was discarded. Its
31	    presence makes a rebuild interrupted mid-copy converge on reopen (the
32	    rebuild is simply repeated) and keeps the reported ``discarded`` count
33	    stable across reopens and repeated recoveries. It is removed by the next
34	    successful commit.
35	
36	Read-only processes (``Store(path, read_only=True)``) take no lock and never
37	create or modify a file. At open each one picks the highest committed prefix
38	available at that instant -- the validated ``wal.log`` prefix or ``wal.ckp``
39	-- scans it once into memory and serves every ``get`` from that index.
40	Because the chosen image is complete and is only ever replaced atomically
41	(never edited in place), a refresh caught mid-rename, a half-written commit,
42	a torn record, or a log being rebuilt, shrunk or compacted can never expose
43	partial bytes: each read lands on one full committed snapshot that was
44	current at or after the open. A directory written by an older version is
45	opened the same way from its log and checkpoint. Reads never replay the log
46	afterwards, so their cost is independent of history and they never block
47	the writer; a reader that is killed or simply hangs changes nothing on disk.
48	
49	Compaction (``Store.compact()``) rewrites the committed history into one
50	tight image without losing a byte of committed state. The compacted log
51	holds exactly the live puts -- one per currently committed key, in sorted
52	key order -- followed by a *base commit* marker carrying the pre-compaction
53	sequence number. The durable sequence keeps that value, so the next commit
54	is ``seq + 1`` and every later commit continues the strict sequence; keys
55	that were deleted never come back. The image is assembled in memory and
56	staged as the atomically replaced ``wal.cmp`` sidecar; finishing installs
57	it as ``wal.ckp`` first and as ``wal.log`` second. Every intermediate state
58	is therefore either the pair of old files or the pair of complete new
59	images, which is precisely the two-image world the reader already chooses
60	between: a kill anywhere leaves a state reopening converges by simply
61	repeating the finish, and interrupting compaction any number of times
62	produces the same bytes as one clean run. Live readers keep serving their
63	pinned old snapshots (the inode survives on Unix; on Windows readers hold
64	no writer-side fd) and new readers land on the new snapshot, never a mix,
65	a half-written file or a byte that was already reclaimed.
66	
67	The durable commit boundary is the highest of the validated log boundary,
68	the checkpoint boundary and the marker boundary, so it can never move
69	backwards. Every repair step is either idempotent or an atomic rename; a
70	kill between any two steps leaves a state the next open converges from to
71	the identical result.
72	
73	Log frame layout (all integers big-endian)::
74	
75	    +---------+----------------+------------+----------------------+---------+
76	    | b"WAL2" | payload_length | header_crc | payload              | crc32   |
77	    | 4 bytes | 8 bytes        | 4 bytes    | metadata\\n<value>    | 4 bytes |
78	    +---------+----------------+------------+----------------------+---------+
79	
80	``header_crc`` is the crc32 of the magic and length bytes. It makes a
81	partial header that borrows bytes from a following frame fail validation,
82	so an incomplete record in the middle of the log reads as corruption while
83	a genuinely short final header reads as a torn tail.
84	
85	Metadata is a compact JSON object: ``{"t":"p","k":key}`` for puts,
86	``{"t":"d","k":key}`` for deletes, ``{"t":"c","s":seq}`` for ordinary
87	commits and ``{"t":"b","s":seq}`` for the base commit that closes a
88	compacted log. The two carry the sequence identically; a base marker is
89	additionally required to be the first commit marker in its file.
90	The raw value bytes follow the first newline, so values need no encoding.
91	"""
92	
93	from __future__ import annotations
94	
95	import io
96	import json
97	import os
98	import sys
99	import zlib
100	
101	__all__ = ["Store", "CorruptLogError", "inject_tear"]
102	
103	
104	class CorruptLogError(ValueError):
105	    """The write-ahead log is corrupt, not merely missing a torn tail.
106	
107	    A single incomplete final record is a normal crash remnant and is
108	    discarded during recovery. Anything else that fails framing, checksum,
109	    metadata or commit-sequence validation is corruption; recovery stops
110	    without applying or removing anything.
111	    """
112	
113	
114	LOG_NAME = "wal.log"
115	_CHECKPOINT_NAME = "wal.ckp"
116	_MARKER_NAME = "wal.rec"
117	_COMPACT_NAME = "wal.cmp"
118	
119	_MAGIC = b"WAL2"
120	_PREFIX = 12  # 4 bytes magic + 8 bytes payload length
121	_HEADER = 16   # prefix + 4 bytes crc32 of the prefix
122	_TRAILER = 4   # crc32 of the payload
123	_MAX_PAYLOAD = 1 << 40
124	
125	_OP_PUT = "p"
126	_OP_DELETE = "d"
127	_OP_COMMIT = "c"
128	_OP_BASE = "b"
129	_COMMIT_OPS = (_OP_COMMIT, _OP_BASE)
130	
131	
132	def _encode_frame(op: str, value: bytes = b"", key: str | None = None,
133	                  seq: int | None = None) -> bytes:
134	    meta: dict[str, object] = {"t": op}
135	    if key is not None:
136	        meta["k"] = key
137	    if seq is not None:
138	        meta["s"] = seq
139	    head = json.dumps(meta, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
140	    payload = head + b"\n" + value
141	    prefix = _MAGIC + len(payload).to_bytes(8, "big")
142	    header = prefix + zlib.crc32(prefix).to_bytes(4, "big")
143	    return header + payload + zlib.crc32(payload).to_bytes(4, "big")
144	
145	
146	def _iter_frames(f):
147	    """Scan an open binary log file from position 0.
148	
149	    For every intact frame yields
150	    ``("frame", meta, value, start, end)``. Scanning stops with either no
151	    terminal event (clean EOF), ``("torn", start)`` for a single incomplete
152	    final frame, or ``("invalid", start)`` for a frame that fails framing,
153	    header/payload checksum or metadata parsing. With the header checksum a
154	    partial header that borrows bytes from a following record cannot survive,
155	    so a short read landing exactly at EOF is reliably the one unfinished
156	    record a single writer was appending when it died; bytes left beyond such
157	    a read instead make it corruption.
158	    """
159	    f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
160	    eof = f.tell()
161	    f.seek(0)
162	    while True:
163	        start = f.tell()
164	        header = f.read(_HEADER)
165	        if not header:
166	            return
167	        if len(header) < _HEADER:
168	            # Trailing bytes of a frame header are a torn tail only when
169	            # nothing follows them; a gap anywhere else is corruption.
170	            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
171	                   else ("invalid", start))
172	            return
173	        if header[:4] != _MAGIC:
174	            yield "invalid", start
175	            return
176	        if int.from_bytes(header[_PREFIX:], "big") != zlib.crc32(
177	                header[:_PREFIX]):
178	            yield "invalid", start
179	            return
180	        length = int.from_bytes(header[4:_PREFIX], "big")
181	        if length > _MAX_PAYLOAD:
182	            yield "invalid", start
183	            return
184	        payload = f.read(length)
185	        checksum = f.read(_TRAILER)
186	        if len(payload) < length or len(checksum) < _TRAILER:
187	            # Only the single final record may be incomplete.
188	            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
189	                   else ("invalid", start))
190	            return
191	        if int.from_bytes(checksum, "big") != zlib.crc32(payload):
192	            yield "invalid", start
193	            return
194	        newline = payload.find(b"\n")
195	        if newline < 0:
196	            yield "invalid", start
197	            return
198	        try:
199	            meta = json.loads(payload[:newline])
200	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
201	            yield "invalid", start
202	            return
203	        if not isinstance(meta, dict) or not isinstance(meta.get("t"), str):
204	            yield "invalid", start
205	            return
206	        yield "frame", meta, payload[newline + 1:], start, f.tell()
207	
208	
209	def _fsync_dir(path: str) -> None:
210	    """Fsync a directory so a nearby rename/unlink is durable.
211	
212	    Windows cannot open directories for fsync and raises ``PermissionError``
213	    (access denied); directory entries there are made durable by the file's
214	    own flush-on-rename, so skipping the directory fsync keeps store creation
215	    working everywhere. Other platforms occasionally refuse the directory
216	    open or the fsync the same way (restrictive mounts, virtualised FSes);
217	    that is likewise best-effort -- the file's own fsync is what carries the
218	    data -- so a ``PermissionError`` at either step never aborts store
219	    creation or a commit/compaction.
220	    """
221	    if sys.platform == "win32":
222	        return
223	    try:
224	        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
225	    except PermissionError:
226	        return
227	    try:
228	        try:
229	            os.fsync(fd)
230	        except PermissionError:
231	            # Some non-Windows mounts reject directory fsync the same way.
232	            pass
233	    finally:
234	        os.close(fd)
235	
236	
237	def _write_all(fd: int, data: bytes) -> None:
238	    view = memoryview(data)
239	    while view:
240	        view = view[os.write(fd, view):]
241	
242	
243	def inject_tear(source, destination, offset):
244	    """Copy a log cut at exactly ``offset`` bytes, for bytewise verification.
245	
246	    Produces ``destination`` containing the first ``offset`` bytes of
247	    ``source`` -- a replica of a process killed precisely when the write had
248	    reached that byte offset. The source file is never modified. Either path
249	    argument may be a store directory, in which case its ``wal.log`` is used.
250	
251	    ``offset`` must satisfy ``0 <= offset <= len(source)``; a negative or
252	    past-the-end offset raises ``IndexError``. The full-length copy
253	    (``offset == len(source)``) is the clean control case.
254	
255	    Verification aid only; the normal write path never calls this.
256	    """
257	    if not isinstance(offset, int) or isinstance(offset, bool):
258	        raise TypeError("offset must be an integer byte offset")
259	
260	    src = os.path.join(source, LOG_NAME) if os.path.isdir(source) else source
261	    dst = (os.path.join(destination, LOG_NAME)
262	           if os.path.isdir(destination) else destination)
263	
264	    size = os.path.getsize(src)
265	    if offset < 0 or offset > size:
266	        raise IndexError(
267	            f"tear offset {offset} out of range for log of {size} bytes")
268	    if os.path.abspath(src) == os.path.abspath(dst):
269	        raise ValueError("tear destination must differ from the source log")
270	
271	    remaining = offset
272	    with open(src, "rb") as fsrc, open(dst, "wb") as fdst:
273	        while remaining:
274	            chunk = fsrc.read(min(remaining, 1 << 20))
275	            if not chunk:  # pragma: no cover - size came from the same file
276	                raise IndexError("source log shrank while copying")
277	            fdst.write(chunk)
278	            remaining -= len(chunk)
279	        fdst.truncate(offset)
280	        os.fsync(fdst.fileno())
281	    return dst

284	class Store:
285	    """A single-writer key value store backed by an append-only log.
286	
287	    ``path`` must be an existing store directory; the log file inside it is
288	    created on first use. Opening a missing directory raises
289	    ``FileNotFoundError`` and opening a path that is not a directory raises
290	    ``OSError``.
291	
292	    With ``read_only=True`` the store is opened purely for reading. No file
293	    is ever created or modified, and no lock is taken: any number of
294	    read-only processes may coexist with the one writer. The reader pins the
295	    committed snapshot current at open time -- the highest committed prefix
296	    of ``wal.log`` or of the atomically replaced ``wal.ckp`` sidecar --
297	    scans it once, and serves every ``get`` from that in-memory index. The
298	    snapshot is independent of the log's later history, so a read never
299	    replays the log and cannot block the writer, and uncommitted bytes, a
300	    half-written commit, a torn record or a half-finished rebuild are never
301	    visible. ``put``, ``delete``, ``commit``, ``recover`` and ``compact``
302	    are rejected on a read-only store; ``stats`` reports the pinned
303	    snapshot.
304	    """
305	
306	    def __init__(self, path: str, read_only: bool = False):
307	        self._dir = path
308	        self._path = os.path.join(path, LOG_NAME)
309	        self._ckp_path = os.path.join(path, _CHECKPOINT_NAME)
310	        self._marker_path = os.path.join(path, _MARKER_NAME)
311	        self._cmp_path = os.path.join(path, _COMPACT_NAME)
312	        self._read_only = read_only
313	
314	        # Recovery needs a directory to replay; a missing target is an error
315	        # at open time, not an implicit create.
316	        if not os.path.exists(path):
317	            raise FileNotFoundError(
318	                f"store directory does not exist: {path!r}")
319	        if not os.path.isdir(path):
320	            raise OSError(f"store path is not a directory: {path!r}")
321	
322	        self._data: dict[str, bytes] = {}
323	        self._seq = 0
324	        self._entries = 0
325	        self._pending = 0
326	        self._closed = False
327	        self._corrupt = False
328	        # Torn records dropped in this recovery epoch; wal.rec carries it
329	        # across processes until the next commit.
330	        self._discarded = 0
331	
332	        if read_only:
333	            # A read-only open holds no writable fd and never takes a lock;
334	            # leave the writer fd slot unset for clarity.
335	            self._fd = -1
336	            self._open_read_only()
337	            return
338	
339	        log_created = not os.path.exists(self._path)
340	        self._fd = os.open(self._path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND,
341	                           0o644)
342	        if log_created:
343	            os.fsync(self._fd)
344	            _fsync_dir(path)
345	
346	        self._converge_on_open()
347	
348	    # -- log scanning and validation --------------------------------------
349	
350	    def _read_log(self, path=None):
351	        frames = []
352	        terminal = None
353	        with open(path or self._path, "rb") as f:
354	            for event in _iter_frames(f):
355	                if event[0] == "frame":
356	                    _, meta, value, start, end = event
357	                    frames.append((meta, value, start, end))
358	                else:
359	                    terminal = event
360	        return frames, terminal
361	
362	    @staticmethod
363	    def _validate(frames, terminal):
364	        """Validate every frame and the strictly increasing commit sequence.
365	
366	        Returns ``(committed_end, last_seq)`` -- the byte offset just past
367	        the last commit marker and its sequence number. An ``"invalid"``
368	        terminal is corruption and raises ``CorruptLogError``; a ``"torn"``
369	        terminal is left for the caller, which decides from the durable
370	        checkpoint whether it is a tail to discard or a gash to restore.
371	
372	        A compacted image starts with a base commit marker (``"b"``) that
373	        carries the pre-compaction sequence: it must be the first commit
374	        marker in the file, it establishes the expected sequence at
375	        ``seq + 1`` and no second base marker may ever follow. An ordinary
376	        first commit must still be sequence 1.
377	        """
378	        expected_seq = 1
379	        last_seq = 0
380	        committed_end = 0
381	        for meta, _value, _start, end in frames:
382	            op = meta.get("t")
383	            if op in (_OP_PUT, _OP_DELETE):
384	                key = meta.get("k")
385	                if not isinstance(key, str) or key == "":
386	                    raise CorruptLogError(
387	                        f"invalid frame metadata: {meta!r}")
388	            elif op == _OP_BASE:
389	                seq = meta.get("s")
390	                if not isinstance(seq, int) or isinstance(seq, bool):
391	                    raise CorruptLogError(
392	                        f"invalid base commit marker: {meta!r}")
393	                if last_seq != 0:
394	                    raise CorruptLogError(
395	                        "base commit must be the first commit marker")
396	                if seq < 1:
397	                    raise CorruptLogError(
398	                        f"base commit sequence {seq} out of order")
399	                last_seq = seq
400	                expected_seq = seq + 1
401	                committed_end = end
402	            elif op == _OP_COMMIT:
403	                seq = meta.get("s")
404	                if not isinstance(seq, int) or isinstance(seq, bool):
405	                    raise CorruptLogError(
406	                        f"invalid commit marker: {meta!r}")
407	                if seq != expected_seq:
408	                    raise CorruptLogError(
409	                        f"commit sequence {seq} out of order, "
410	                        f"expected {expected_seq}")
411	                last_seq = seq
412	                expected_seq += 1
413	                committed_end = end
414	            else:
415	                raise CorruptLogError(f"unknown frame type: {op!r}")
416	        if terminal is not None and terminal[0] == "invalid":
417	            raise CorruptLogError("corrupt log frame")
418	        return committed_end, last_seq
419	
420	    @staticmethod
421	    def _replay(frames) -> tuple[dict[str, bytes], int]:
422	        state: dict[str, bytes] = {}
423	        applied = 0
424	        for meta, value, _start, _end in frames:
425	            op = meta["t"]
426	            if op in _COMMIT_OPS:
427	                continue
428	            if op == _OP_PUT:
429	                state[meta["k"]] = value
430	            else:  # _OP_DELETE
431	                state.pop(meta["k"], None)
432	            applied += 1
433	        return state, applied
434	
435	    @staticmethod
436	    def _last_seq(frames) -> int:
437	        return max(
438	            (meta["s"] for meta, _v, _s, _e in frames
439	             if meta.get("t") in _COMMIT_OPS),
440	            default=0)
441	
442	    # -- crash-convergence sidecars ---------------------------------------
443	
444	    @staticmethod
445	    def _copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, length: int) -> None:
446	        remaining = length
447	        while remaining:
448	            chunk = fsrc.read(min(remaining, 1 << 20))
449	            if not chunk:
450	                raise CorruptLogError(
451	                    "source ended before the committed prefix")
452	            fdst.write(chunk)
453	            remaining -= len(chunk)
454	        fdst.truncate(length)
455	
456	    def _atomic_file(self, target: str, write) -> None:
457	        """Replace ``target`` atomically: temp file, fsync, rename, dir fsync."""
458	        tmp = target + ".tmp"
459	        with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
460	            write(f)
461	            os.fsync(f.fileno())
462	        os.replace(tmp, target)
463	        _fsync_dir(self._dir)
464	
465	    def _write_checkpoint(self, end: int) -> None:
466	        """Persist the log prefix ``[0, end)`` as the clean checkpoint."""
467	        if end <= 0:
468	            return
469	
470	        def write(fdst):
471	            with open(self._path, "rb") as fsrc:
472	                self._copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, end)
473	
474	        self._atomic_file(self._ckp_path, write)
475	
476	    def _checkpoint_boundary(self) -> int:
477	        """Commit boundary the durable checkpoint covers; 0 if absent.
478	
479	        A checkpoint that is torn, unparseable or not exactly one committed
480	        prefix is corruption of the recovery machinery rather than a discard.
481	        """
482	        try:
483	            frames, terminal = self._read_log(self._ckp_path)
484	        except FileNotFoundError:
485	            return 0
486	        if not frames:
487	            # An empty checkpoint covers the empty prefix; anything non-empty
488	            # that parses to no frames is corruption.
489	            if os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path) == 0 and terminal is None:
490	                return 0
491	            raise CorruptLogError("checkpoint is not a clean committed prefix")
492	        if terminal is not None:
493	            raise CorruptLogError("checkpoint is not a clean committed prefix")
494	        end, _seq = self._validate(frames, None)
495	        if end != os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path):
496	            raise CorruptLogError("checkpoint has bytes past its commit")
497	        return end
498	
499	    def _write_marker(self, clean_end: int, discarded: int) -> None:
500	        payload = json.dumps(
501	            {"end": clean_end, "discarded": discarded},
502	            separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
503	
504	        def write(f):
505	            f.write(payload)
506	
507	        self._atomic_file(self._marker_path, write)
508	
509	    def _read_marker(self):
510	        try:
511	            with open(self._marker_path, "rb") as f:
512	                raw = f.read()
513	        except FileNotFoundError:
514	            return None
515	        try:
516	            marker = json.loads(raw)
517	            end = marker["end"]
518	            discarded = marker["discarded"]
519	        except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError):
520	            raise CorruptLogError("unparseable recovery marker")
521	        if (not isinstance(end, int) or isinstance(end, bool) or end < 0
522	                or discarded not in (0, 1)):
523	            raise CorruptLogError("invalid recovery marker")
524	        return end, discarded
525	
526	    def _remove_marker(self) -> None:
527	        try:
528	            os.unlink(self._marker_path)
529	        except FileNotFoundError:
530	            return
531	        _fsync_dir(self._dir)
532	
533	    def _remove_stale_temps(self) -> None:
534	        for name in (self._path + ".tmp", self._ckp_path + ".tmp",
535	                     self._marker_path + ".tmp", self._cmp_path + ".tmp"):
536	            try:
537	                os.unlink(name)
538	            except FileNotFoundError:
539	                pass
540	
541	    def _rebuild_log(self, clean_end: int) -> None:
542	        """Make the log exactly its clean ``[0, clean_end)`` prefix.
543	
544	        Kill-safe and idempotent: when a checkpoint covers the prefix the new
545	        log is fully written and fsynced as a temp file and atomically renamed
546	        over the old one, so a kill leaves either the old log or the complete
547	        restored log -- never a half-written file -- and rerunning converges.
548	        Without a checkpoint but with the committed bytes still at stable
549	        offsets, a synced truncate drops the tail instead. The empty prefix is
550	        a truncate to zero.
551	        """
552	        size = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size
553	        if size == clean_end:
554	            return
555	
556	        if clean_end == 0:
557	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, 0)
558	            os.fsync(self._fd)
559	            return
560	
561	        try:
562	            ckp_size = os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path)
563	        except FileNotFoundError:
564	            ckp_size = -1
565	
566	        if ckp_size < clean_end and size > clean_end:
567	            # No checkpoint, but the committed bytes survive at stable
568	            # offsets: drop the dirty tail. Idempotent if killed mid-call.
569	            try:
570	                os.fsync(self._fd)
571	            except OSError:
572	                pass
573	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, clean_end)
574	            os.fsync(self._fd)
575	            return
576	        if ckp_size < clean_end:
577	            raise CorruptLogError(
578	                "committed prefix is torn and no checkpoint covers it")
579	
580	        tmp = self._path + ".tmp"
581	        with open(self._ckp_path, "rb") as fsrc, open(tmp, "wb") as fdst:
582	            self._copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, clean_end)
583	            os.fsync(fdst.fileno())
584	        # Windows cannot rename over a path held open by the append fd.
585	        os.close(self._fd)
586	        try:
587	            os.replace(tmp, self._path)
588	            _fsync_dir(self._dir)
589	        finally:
590	            self._fd = os.open(
591	                self._path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
592	        if os.fstat(self._fd).st_size != clean_end:
593	            raise CorruptLogError("restore did not converge")

595	    # -- compaction --------------------------------------------------------
596	
597	    def _build_compact_image(self, seq: int) -> tuple[bytes, int]:
598	        """Serialise the committed state into one compact log image.
599	
600	        One put frame per live key, keys in sorted order, followed by a base
601	        commit marker carrying the pre-compaction sequence. The empty state
602	        at seq 0 is an empty image rather than a zero-sequence marker.
603	        """
604	        if seq == 0:
605	            return b"", 0
606	        parts = [_encode_frame(_OP_PUT, value, key=key)
607	                 for key, value in sorted(self._data.items())]
608	        parts.append(_encode_frame(_OP_BASE, seq=seq))
609	        return b"".join(parts), len(self._data)
610	
611	    def _read_compact_candidate(self):
612	        """Validate ``wal.cmp`` as one compacted image.
613	
614	        Returns ``(image, end, seq, live)`` where ``image`` is the exact
615	        byte content, or ``None`` when the sidecar is absent. The image must
616	        be a clean file ending exactly on a base commit marker, preceded only
617	        by put frames with strictly increasing keys; anything else is
618	        corruption of the crash-convergence machinery, never a discardable
619	        tail (the sidecar is always atomically replaced, never written in
620	        place).
621	        """
622	        try:
623	            f = open(self._cmp_path, "rb")
624	        except FileNotFoundError:
625	            return None
626	        with f:
627	            image = f.read()
628	        if not image:
629	            # An empty candidate encodes the empty state at seq 0.
630	            return b"", 0, 0, 0
631	
632	        frames, terminal = self._scan_bytes(image)
633	        if terminal is not None:
634	            raise CorruptLogError(
635	                "compaction candidate is not a clean committed prefix")
636	        end, seq = self._validate(frames, None)
637	        if end != len(image) or seq <= 0:
638	            raise CorruptLogError(
639	                "compaction candidate has bytes past its base commit")
640	        live = 0
641	        last_key: str | None = None
642	        saw_base = False
643	        for meta, _value, _start, _end in frames:
644	            op = meta.get("t")
645	            if op == _OP_PUT:
646	                if saw_base:
647	                    raise CorruptLogError(
648	                        "compaction candidate has puts past its base commit")
649	                key = meta["k"]
650	                if last_key is not None and key <= last_key:
651	                    raise CorruptLogError(
652	                        "compaction candidate keys are not sorted uniquely")
653	                last_key = key
654	                live += 1
655	            elif op == _OP_BASE:
656	                if saw_base:
657	                    raise CorruptLogError(
658	                        "compaction candidate has multiple base commits")
659	                saw_base = True
660	            else:
661	                raise CorruptLogError(
662	                    "compaction candidate contains a non-compacted frame")
663	        if not saw_base:
664	            raise CorruptLogError(
665	                "compaction candidate ends without a base commit")
666	        return image, end, seq, live
667	
668	    def _scan_bytes(self, data: bytes):
669	        """Frame-scan raw bytes as if they were a log file."""
670	        frames = []
671	        terminal = None
672	        with io.BytesIO(data) as f:
673	            for event in _iter_frames(f):
674	                if event[0] == "frame":
675	                    _, meta, value, start, end = event
676	                    frames.append((meta, value, start, end))
677	                else:
678	                    terminal = event
679	        return frames, terminal
680	
681	    def _install_log_bytes(self, image: bytes) -> None:
682	        """Atomically replace the log with ``image`` and reopen the fd.
683	
684	        The complete image is written and fsynced as a temp file first, so a
685	        kill leaves either the old log or the complete new one -- never a
686	        half-written log. The append fd is closed for the rename because
687	        Windows cannot replace a path held open by it, then reopened.
688	        """
689	        tmp = self._path + ".tmp"
690	        with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
691	            f.write(image)
692	            f.truncate(len(image))
693	            os.fsync(f.fileno())
694	        os.close(self._fd)
695	        try:
696	            os.replace(tmp, self._path)
697	            _fsync_dir(self._dir)
698	        finally:
699	            self._fd = os.open(
700	                self._path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
701	        if os.fstat(self._fd).st_size != len(image):
702	            raise CorruptLogError("compaction did not converge")
703	
704	    def _install_compaction(self, image: bytes, seq: int) -> None:
705	        """Publish a staged compacted image; idempotent and kill-safe.
706	
707	        The torn-tail marker is dropped first: its byte offset belongs to
708	        the old (longer) log and must not outlive the shrink. Checkpoint is
709	        replaced next and the log last, both via complete-file atomic
710	        renames, then the candidate is removed. Any ordering of a kill
711	        between those steps leaves the durable files equal to either the old
712	        pair or the complete new pair, and rerunning (via the surviving
713	        candidate) converges to the same compacted bytes.
714	        """
715	        # Compaction closes any prior recovery epoch the way a commit does;
716	        # do it while the old log still exists so a later kill replays this
717	        # whole publish from the durable candidate.
718	        self._remove_marker()
719	
720	        if seq == 0:
721	            # Empty committed state: the log is zero length and there is no
722	            # checkpoint to publish; reclaim every old byte and drop the plan.
723	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, 0)
724	            os.fsync(self._fd)
725	            try:
726	                os.unlink(self._ckp_path)
727	                _fsync_dir(self._dir)
728	            except FileNotFoundError:
729	                pass
730	            self._remove_candidate()
731	            return
732	
733	        def write(fdst):
734	            fdst.write(image)
735	
736	        self._atomic_file(self._ckp_path, write)
737	        self._install_log_bytes(image)
738	        self._remove_candidate()
739	
740	    def _remove_candidate(self) -> None:
741	        try:
742	            os.unlink(self._cmp_path)
743	        except FileNotFoundError:
744	            return
745	        _fsync_dir(self._dir)
746	
747	    def _finish_compaction(self) -> None:
748	        """Complete a compaction interrupted after its candidate went durable.
749	
750	        With a single writer a present candidate means its compaction never
751	        finished (no later commit was possible), so the log and checkpoint
752	        cannot be ahead of it; the publish is simply repeated. A candidate
753	        whose boundary a newer durable epoch has overtaken is stale and is
754	        discarded instead.
755	        """
756	        candidate = self._read_compact_candidate()
757	        if candidate is None:
758	            return
759	        image, _end, cand_seq, _live = candidate
760	
761	        log_seq = 0
762	        if os.path.exists(self._path):
763	            frames, terminal = self._read_log(self._path)
764	            _log_end, log_seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
765	        ckp_seq = 0
766	        ckp = self._read_clean_prefix(self._ckp_path)
767	        if ckp is not None:
768	            _frames, _end, ckp_seq = ckp
769	        if max(log_seq, ckp_seq) > cand_seq:
770	            # A newer committed epoch exists; the staged image is obsolete.
771	            self._remove_candidate()
772	            return
773	        self._install_compaction(image, cand_seq)
774	
775	    def _converge(self):
776	        """Validate and converge the on-disk log to its clean state.
777	
778	        Returns ``(frames, discarded)`` for the now-clean log. Raises
779	        ``CorruptLogError`` without changing anything if the log is corrupt.
780	        Safe to run repeatedly and safe to kill at any point.
781	
782	        The durable commit boundary is the highest of the validated log
783	        boundary, the checkpoint boundary and the marker boundary, so it can
784	        never regress. A log torn inside its committed prefix is rebuilt from
785	        the checkpoint and ``discarded`` stays 0 (those bytes were committed,
786	        not an unfinished write); a torn or merely uncommitted tail past the
787	        boundary is discarded, and the marker freezes that report until the
788	        next commit even when the kill lands mid-repair.
789	        """
790	        self._remove_stale_temps()
791	        # A durable compaction candidate left by a killed compact() is
792	        # published before ordinary convergence; it is itself a complete
793	        # committed prefix, so this never invents or loses a committed byte.
794	        self._finish_compaction()
795	        marker = self._read_marker()
796	        marker_end = -1
797	        marker_discarded = 0
798	        if marker is not None:
799	            marker_end, marker_discarded = marker
800	
801	        frames, terminal = self._read_log()
802	        log_end, _log_seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
803	        ckp_end = self._checkpoint_boundary()
804	        size = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size
805	
806	        target = max(log_end, ckp_end, marker_end)
807	        # The target bytes must come from somewhere still on disk: the
808	        # validated log itself or the checkpoint.
809	        if target > log_end and target > ckp_end:
810	            raise CorruptLogError("recovery target has no durable source")
811	
812	        log_clean = terminal is None and size == log_end
813	
814	        if log_clean and log_end == target:
815	            # Nothing to repair. An old marker whose epoch a newer commit
816	            # closed durably can finally go; otherwise its discarded count
817	            # stays frozen until that commit.
818	            if marker is not None:
819	                if target > marker_end:
820	                    self._remove_marker()
821	                    discarded = 0
822	                else:
823	                    discarded = marker_discarded
824	            else:
825	                discarded = 0
826	            if ckp_end < target:
827	                self._write_checkpoint(target)
828	            return frames, discarded
829	
830	        if target > log_end:
831	            # Committed bytes were torn away (offset 0 included): the
832	            # checkpoint is the source of truth. The discarded count is only
833	            # meaningful when the marker pins this exact boundary.
834	            discarded = marker_discarded if target == marker_end else 0
835	            self._rebuild_log(target)
836	        else:
837	            # A dirty suffix sits past the boundary. Decide discarded from
838	            # the suffix itself: a torn final record counts, complete
839	            # uncommitted frames do not. This also covers a repair killed
840	            # before the rebuild (the original suffix is still here, so the
841	            # same decision is reached) and fresh writes appended after a
842	            # previous repair (a new crash is a new decision rather than the
843	            # old marker's). A marker is only frozen once the log itself is
844	            # rebuilt clean; see the clean branch above.
845	            discarded = 1 if terminal is not None else 0
846	            if ckp_end < target:
847	                # Make the prefix independently restorable before we publish
848	                # the plan or remove any bytes.
849	                self._write_checkpoint(target)
850	            self._write_marker(target, discarded)
851	            self._rebuild_log(target)
852	
853	        frames, terminal = self._read_log()
854	        end, _seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
855	        if end != target or terminal is not None:
856	            raise CorruptLogError("restore did not converge")
857	        return frames, discarded
858	
859	    def _publish(self, frames, discarded) -> None:
860	        state, _applied = self._replay(frames)
861	        self._data = state
862	        self._seq = self._last_seq(frames)
863	        self._entries = len(frames)
864	        self._pending = 0
865	        self._discarded = discarded
866	        self._corrupt = False
867	
868	    def _converge_on_open(self) -> None:
869	        """Crash cleanup at open; leave a corrupt store inert for recover()."""
870	        try:
871	            frames, discarded = self._converge()
872	        except CorruptLogError:
873	            self._corrupt = True
874	            return
875	        self._publish(frames, discarded)
